section: Kits: Python, Swift, Bash, and SQL
finding: | `packages/cli/kits/language/python/basedpyrightconfig.json.tmpl:2-108` (no `venvPath`, `venv`) | The configuration names no interpreter. gspot runs basedpyright from `.gspot/.venv` (`packages/cli/src/tools/locate.ts:26`) and sets no `VIRTUAL_ENV`. In a sample, a package installed in the project's `.venv` gave `reportMissingImports`, which is an error at both levels. Adding `venvPath` and `venv` cleared it. In a hook or CI shell with no active environment, every third-party import fails `python/basedpyright`. | When the scope has a `.venv`, write `"venvPath"` and `"venv"`. Add a setting for projects that keep the interpreter somewhere else. |

section: Kits: Python, Swift, Bash, and SQL
finding: | `packages/cli/kits/language/python/manifest.toml:142-154` (import-linter), `:171-184` (deptry) | Both run from gspot's environment, so they cannot see the project's installed packages. In a sample, declaring `beautifulsoup4` and importing `bs4` gave DEP001 and DEP002, because deptry cannot map the package name to the module name. lint-imports needs the project's packages to be importable, so a project with a `src` folder fails. | Run both with the project's interpreter, for example through `uv run --project <scope>`. |

section: Kits: Python, Swift, Bash, and SQL
finding: | `packages/cli/kits/language/python/ruff.toml.tmpl:4`, `basedpyrightconfig.json.tmpl:108`, `manifest.toml:194` | Three hard-coded folder lists differ from each other, and none of them reads the root `exclude`, `generated`, or `vendored` settings. basedpyright and vulture scan the whole scope. I found no later step that drops findings in generated files, so a generated `_pb2.py` is type checked. Ruff's `exclude` line replaces Ruff's default list and drops `venv`, `.tox`, `.nox`, and `.eggs`. Because gspot passes file names to Ruff, the line has no effect when gspot runs Ruff. | Build one skip list from the root settings and each language kit's build folders, and use it in all three. Delete Ruff's `exclude` line, or change it to `extend-exclude`. |

section: Kits: Python, Swift, Bash, and SQL
finding: | `packages/cli/kits/language/swift/swiftlint.yml.tmpl:74-83` (`doc_comment_style`) | A custom regex rule bans `/** */` comments. SwiftFormat's opt-in rule `blockComments` does the same and also fixes the comment. | At `all`, turn on `--enable blockComments`, and delete the custom rule. |
decisionEvidence: User plan: Finish all findings with only recommended and all, Decisions. These are the only developer-facing coverage levels. Do not introduce opt-in configurations, profiles, bundles, or extra enabling flags. Generate native selections from the level; retain actual platform, network, build, and project-setting prerequisites.

Implementation owner: packages/cli/src/execution/planning/skips.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/init/prepare.ts, and packages/cli/src/parsers/schema/configurations/manifest.ts. Native SwiftLint opt_in_rules is generated syntax, not another Gspot selection choice.

section: Kits: Python, Swift, Bash, and SQL
finding: | `packages/cli/kits/language/swift/manifest.toml:62-64,119-158`, `packages/cli/src/checks/language/swift/plan.ts:31-39` | When `tools.xcode.project` is not set, the build, the analyzer, and Periphery run `swift build`, and nothing checks that the scope has a `Package.swift`. A scope with Swift files but no package then gets a tool error at push instead of a skip. Examples are an app whose Xcode settings are not set, or a React Native `AppDelegate.swift`. `platforms = ["macos"]` skips `swift build` on Linux, where it works, so a server-side Swift package gets no type check in Linux CI. The kit declares `xcodebuild` as a host tool but not `swift`. | Skip with a message that names `tools.xcode.project` when the scope has no `Package.swift`. Allow `linux` for the package build. Declare `swift` as a host tool. |

section: Kits: Python, Swift, Bash, and SQL
finding: | `packages/cli/kits/language/swift/manifest.toml:34-60` (`swiftformat`, `periphery` tools) | Neither tool has a `suppression` marker. So `// swiftformat:disable` and `// periphery:ignore` escape the reason rule that applies to SwiftLint, Ruff, basedpyright, ShellCheck, and sqlfluff comments. The Periphery help text even tells users to add `periphery:ignore`. | Add `suppression` markers with reason patterns for both tools. |
